top_categories.workout_context: 92ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Vosges. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 110 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Vosges' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
At Gran Fondo Vosges, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 110, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Vosges. Train it until it feels boring.
10,128ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
10,128ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Vosges. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 110 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 10,128ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Vosges’s 110 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Gran Fondo Vosges. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gran Fondo Vosges rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Road Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 110 miles of mixed terrain in La Bresse Hohneck ski station, Vosges, France.
